raw.transcript: No problem. If you don’t know the router password, first check the sticker on the router itself. A lot of routers have the default username and password printed right on the back or bottom. If that’s not there, try the common defaults like “admin” and “admin,” or “admin” and “password.” If those don’t work, look up your router’s model online and find the default login for that exact model. If it’s already been changed and you can’t recover it, you may need to reset the router using the tiny reset button, usually held down for about 10 seconds, but that will wipe custom settings. After that, you can log in with the defaults and set a new password.
